axes.label: Confirmation
axes.title: The Lawyer
axes.desc: You tend to look for what proves you right and skim past what doesn't. That's not a flaw in you, it's how every human brain works. The fix: before you're convinced, go find the strongest argument against you.

axes.label: Anchoring
axes.title: The First-Number Believer
axes.desc: The first number you hear becomes your starting point, even if someone made it up. Salespeople know this well. The fix: decide on your number before you hear theirs.

axes.label: Framing
axes.title: The Phrasing Follower
axes.desc: Say the same fact two different ways and your decision changes. The fix: flip the sentence in your head. "90% success" is the same thing as "10% failure."

axes.label: Sunk Cost
axes.title: The Loyal-to-the-Past
axes.desc: It's hard for you to walk away from something you've put money or time into, even after it's become a loss. The fix: ask yourself, "If I were starting from zero today, would I choose this?"

axes.label: Bandwagon
axes.title: The Crowd Follower
axes.desc: The people around you sway you more than you'd think. The fix: before you get in line, ask, "Do they know something I don't, or is everyone just following everyone else?"

balanced.title: The Steady Scale
balanced.desc: Your answers are balanced, and no single bias runs the show. That doesn't mean you're immune. It means you're paying attention, and that's the most important step.

items.scene: You read a story from a page you've never heard of, but it backs up something you've believed for years.
opts: Share it. It's exactly what I've been saying.
Share it, but add that I'm not sure about the source.
Look for a second source before I share.

items.scene: Someone makes a strong argument against your view on a topic you care about.
opts: Hunt for any mistake in what they said so I can fire back.
Listen, and tell myself I'll think about it later.
Ask myself: if this argument were on my side, would I accept it?

items.scene: You really want a certain phone, and you're checking what people think of it.
opts: Look for the reviews that praise it.
Read whatever reviews I come across.
Go looking specifically for the worst reviews.

items.scene: A salesperson tells you this jacket is $300, then says, "For you, $150."
opts: $150 is a steal. I'll take it.
Haggle a little down from $150.
Ask myself: if I'd never heard $300, what would I say it's worth?

items.scene: A friend tells you apartments in this neighborhood rent for $2,800 a month. You find one for $1,700.
opts: That's a deal. I'm signing today.
Go see it in person first.
Check other listings myself before I decide it's cheap.

items.scene: You're buying a used car, and the seller opens with a really high price.
opts: Start haggling down from his price.
Counter with something close to half.
Look up market prices, and open with my own number.

items.scene: A package of ground beef says: "90% fat-free."
opts: Sounds healthy. I'll buy it.
Seems fine, but I'll check the price.
So it's 10% fat. I'll compare it with the others.

items.scene: A headline says: "Half of students failed this year's math exam."
opts: Education is officially broken.
The test must have been hard.
So half of them passed. I need to know what the rate was in past years.

items.scene: Your banking app says: "You're losing $10 every month by not opening a savings account."
opts: Open one right now. I don't want to lose money.
Think about it.
That's the same as "you could earn $10." I'll decide based on the numbers and the terms.

items.scene: You paid $18 for a movie ticket. Half an hour in, it's painfully boring.
opts: Stay. I already paid for it.
Stay and scroll on my phone.
Leave. The money's gone either way, so I won't waste my time too.

items.scene: You're two years into a long program, and you've realized you don't like it and won't work in that field.
opts: Finish it. I'm not throwing away two years.
Finish it, and look for an alternative on the side.
Decide based on what's ahead: which path is better from today, no matter what came before.

items.scene: You've had your car repaired 3 times in 6 months, and the same problem is back.
opts: Fix it again. I've already spent so much on it.
Fix it this one last time.
Compare the cost of the next repair with selling it.

items.scene: A new restaurant has a long line out the door. The one next to it is empty.
opts: Get in line. It must be better.
Get in line and see.
Check both places' reviews and menus first.

items.scene: There's a trending pile-on, and everyone is going after one person.
opts: Join in. Everyone agrees.
Watch without joining.
Find out the whole story first.

items.scene: In a meeting, everyone agrees on an idea, but you see a problem with it.
opts: Go along with it. I must be the one who's wrong.
Stay quiet.
Calmly point out the problem.
